Subject: Question: heartbeat truncation and minimal billing crediting

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — GreenGrid is excited about the performance numbers. Before we move to procurement, procurement wanted a clear example of how Redwood charges for short-lived bursts where a long prefix is reused across many small calls. Two specific questions: 

1) If a user has a 10k-token conversation stored as a prefix and then makes 20 short 15-token calls that reuse that prefix via KV cache/heartbeat, how does that map to billing units? Do you charge for the full 10k each call, or is there an amortization / heartbeat credit?

2) When streaming/truncation occurs (we truncate prior context on the server to keep latency), how does rounding and the minimum billing floor interact with truncation? E.g., do truncated tokens still count in the same billing window?

Procurement also asked for a sample invoice that shows the math and any credits applied (they asked for a Q2 example). Can you send a simple worked example + the invoice stub?

Appreciate it — Alice
Head of Integrations, GreenGrid

Hi Alice — quick ack and will follow up with the worked example and invoice stub by EOD tomorrow. Short answers up front:

- We do NOT charge the full 10k for every short call. Redwood applies a heartbeat/prefix amortization: long-prefix cost is amortized across active sessions that reuse the prefix within a rolling window (default 30 minutes) and then a smaller heartbeat fee if the prefix remains warm beyond that.

- Truncation on the server removes context from the execution path; billing uses the tokens actually materialized during inference. If we evict parts of the prefix before the call is executed, those evicted tokens will not be billed again — but if the prefix is retained in KV and used, we count those tokens in the request's effective input length for token accounting.

I'll attach a sample invoice + a spreadsheet with the calc and two scenarios (bursty reuse vs. immediate eviction) so procurement can see the numeric difference.

Couple of things for the worked example — can you confirm the monthly commit level (approx tokens / month) or whether GreenGrid would like us to model this as pay-as-you-go? Also confirming procurement email to send the invoice stub to procurement@greengrid.com.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Alice — adding a couple clarifying Notes (technical + billing):

• Amortization window: by default 30 minutes rolling. If your application keeps a conversation cold (evicting KV between requests), amortization does not apply. In that case each call will pay for tokens materialized at inference time.

• Minimum floor / rounding: we meter to the nearest 100-token quantum for per-call billable inputs, with a per-request minimum of 200 tokens (this is configurable for enterprise pilots). We also apply a prefix-reuse credit that reduces repeat-read charges when same KV pages are reused (that credit is shown as a line-item on invoices).

• Truncation: if a truncated prefix is evicted before request execution, it will not be billed. If truncation occurs only logically (we stop using older tokens) but the KV cache still holds the data and it is read during attention or returned to the runtime, those tokens count toward that call's billable input.

I'll put the worked math into the spreadsheet but here's a tiny worked example inline so procurement gets the intuition: 

Scenario A — Prefix warm (KV retained), amortization window active- Long prefix: 10,000 tokens (stored once)- 20 short calls over 10 minutes, each adds 15 tokens of new input = 20 * 15 = 300 tokens new- Metering: initial materialization of prefix amortized across calls -> prefix cost considered 10,000 amortized across active callers (we show as 10,000/20 = 500 tokens per call for the period)- Per-call tokens billed: amortized prefix (500) + new input (15) -> 515 -> rounded to nearest 100 -> 600 tokens charged per call -> 20 calls = 12,000 tokens billed

Scenario B — Prefix evicted between calls (cold read each time)- Each call materializes 10,000 + 15 = 10,015 tokens -> rounded to 10,100 (nearest 100) -> subject to per-request minimum ignored because > minimum- 20 calls = 202,000 tokens billed

Net: same observable workload but orders-of-magnitude difference depending on whether prefix is held warm. We'll include both scenarios in the spreadsheet.

—Kim
Billing & Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Hi Procurement / Alice — attaching the Q2 sample invoice stub and the calculation sheet (heartbeat-credit-calcs.xlsx) to illustrate both scenarios. I've pasted the short summary below and included a link to the spreadsheet in case you want to try alternate amortization windows.

Summary (attached spreadsheet):
- Scenario A (warm prefix, default 30m amortization): total billed tokens = 12,000 -> equivalent charge shown as:
  • Model usage (amortized prefix + per-call input): 12,000 tokens
  • Prefix reuse credit: -9,000 tokens (shown as negative line item)
  • Net billed tokens: 3,000 -> invoice line-item shows net token charge and USD per-token cost.
- Scenario B (cold each call): total billed tokens = 202,000 -> no prefix-reuse credit applied.

Answers:
1) Amortization window: Yes, tunable on enterprise pilots — GreenGrid can pick 5/15/30 minute windows. We can also configure a shorter TTL for KV retention to force earlier eviction if you prefer lower warm-prefix exposure.
2) Rounding deltas: Our invoice groups by route/model and aggregates before rounding (we round at the invoice-line granularity, not per-call on the invoice). That reduces visible variance from small microcalls. We will include per-route line items in the sample invoice for clarity.

Attached: sample_invoice_q2.pdf, heartbeat-credit-calcs.xlsx

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk procurement through the sheet next week.

Best,
